strengths: Novel problem formulation addressing an under-explored setting (panoramic SSC for legged robots) with clear articulation of why existing methods fail

Well-justified technical design: DP-ER sensibly balances raw geometry with convolution-friendly projections; BGV elegantly solves near/far trade-offs; GDC avoids quantization artifacts; all components validated via thorough ablation (Table 4)

Valuable dataset contributions: QuadOcc (first real panoramic occupancy benchmark on quadruped, 24K frames, 10 scenes) and H3O (large-scale CARLA-based with within-/cross-city splits, 8K frames, 16 maps) enable systematic future research
Strong experimental results outperforming LiDAR (20.56 vs 18.44 mIoU on QuadOcc) and vision baselines (37.29 vs 33.46 on H3O within-city), with comprehensive analysis across lighting conditions
Practical efficiency (~14 FPS on RTX-4090, ~19 FPS FP16, >10 FPS extrapolated on Jetson Thor) enables onboard deployment on resource-constrained platforms
Clear presentation with well-motivated design principles, informative pipeline diagram (Figure 2), and thorough ablations demonstrating incremental gains per component
weaknesses: Severely limited real-world validation: QuadOcc contains only 10 scenes from single campus domain, raising critical generalization concerns; no cross-platform validation despite explicit humanoid claims; no evidence of actual humanoid robot testing

Unaddressed calibration dependency: method requires accurate calibration with bounded drift; proposed remedy ('online extrinsic self-calibration') is vague and relegated to future work; no robustness evaluation to calibration errors

Insufficient analysis of key design choices: gradient-energy gating criterion (Eq. 13) lacks theoretical justification or alternative comparison; GDC's modest +0.39 mIoU gain without analysis of learned patterns or applicability conditions; no ablation on voxel grid sensitivity

Incomplete robustness analysis: OneOcc underperforms MonoScene at night (13.50 vs 14.20 mIoU) with shallow explanation; significant cross-city degradation (37.29→32.23, -13.7%) lacks investigation; no per-class depth or occlusion-specific evaluation

Limited baseline comparisons: no evaluation against other panoramic/omnidirectional methods (OmniOcc, panoramic depth); most baselines adapted from pinhole-camera driving datasets (unfair); missing empirical validation that DP-ER outperforms ER-only baseline

Dataset limitations undermining generalization claims: QuadOcc ground truth semi-automatic with unvalidated manual annotations; H3O's 'simulated gait' realism undemonstrated; QuadOcc's single-domain campus setting insufficient for robustness; no evidence method transfers to outdoor autonomous driving scenarios

Humanoid applicability claims unsupported: paper claims applicability to humanoid robots but provides no testing, evaluation, or analysis of bipedal motion; GDC (designed for quadruped gait) never validated on different morphologies

Technical gaps: per-voxel fusion weights (Eq. 7) learning mechanism unspecified; relation loss omission justified only by vague 'over-smoothing' observation; evaluation metric (mIoU on non-empty voxels only) may bias toward common classes; some design choices lack ablation (MLP architecture, scale weights)

strengths: Addresses an important and underexplored problem—semantic occupancy prediction for legged robots with single panoramic cameras—with clear motivation distinguishing legged from wheeled platforms
Introduces two valuable datasets (QuadOcc: real quadruped data; Human360Occ: comprehensive CARLA-based benchmark) that will enable future research on panoramic perception for embodied AI

Technically sound method integrating well-motivated components: DP-ER exploits complementary geometric properties of raw and equirectangular projections; BGV naturally balances Cartesian (near-field) and cylindrical-polar (far-field ring) reasoning; novel gradient-energy gating in AMoE-3D emphasizes structural boundaries

Strong empirical results surpassing LiDAR baselines on real data (20.56 vs. 18.44 mIoU QuadOcc) and showing substantial cross-domain robustness on H3O (37.29/32.23 within/cross-city, +8.08 on cross-city)

Comprehensive experimental validation including ablations, qualitative comparisons, lighting robustness analysis, and efficiency evaluation demonstrating practical deployment feasibility (14-18 FPS on RTX 4090)
Clear presentation with well-motivated design choices, informative visualizations, and thorough related work positioning
weaknesses: Limited real-world data scope: QuadOcc contains only 10 scenes from single campus domain with one quadruped platform, raising significant generalization concerns to diverse terrains, other legged morphologies (hexapods, bipeds), and varied environments

Ground truth annotation quality lacks validation: semi-automatic pipeline (LiDAR aggregation → Grounded-SAM → 'targeted manual fixes') provides no inter-rater agreement statistics or consistency analysis, potentially introducing systematic biases into performance metrics

Gait Displacement Compensation shows modest gains (+0.39 mIoU), suggesting either jitter is less problematic than motivated or compensation mechanism is insufficient; no direct validation against measured gait patterns or temporal periodicity modeling

Methodological inconsistency: H3O experiments disable raw-projection branch (contradicting core DP-ER design), and loss function excludes relation loss specifically for panoramic data, suggesting configuration tuning is dataset-specific rather than universally applicable

Insufficient ablation analysis: Table 4 doesn't isolate gradient-energy gating vs. attention, hierarchical vs. single-level injection, or cross-grid fusion impact separately, leaving architectural choices incompletely justified

No experiments validating robustness to calibration errors despite acknowledging 'bounded drift' dependency; no online re-calibration mechanism despite practical importance for long-term legged robot deployment
Limited baseline coverage: no quantitative comparison with other panoramic/omnidirectional methods (OmniOcc, OccCylindrical); most adapted methods (MonoScene, VoxFormer) designed for pinhole cameras

Cross-domain concerns: large within/cross-city gap on H3O (37.29→32.23) suggests environment-specific overfitting; no evaluation on alternative quadruped morphologies, gaits, or humanoid platforms; night performance lags baseline (13.50 vs. 14.20 MonoScene)

Reproducibility limitations: code/datasets promised but unavailable at review; missing implementation details (encoder architecture, hyperparameter selection rationale, training time, convergence behavior) limit verification

Incomplete failure analysis: no discussion of failure modes (transparent surfaces, reflective materials, extreme motion), no per-class performance breakdown on challenging scenarios, and computational requirements insufficient to claim 'lightweight' for all platforms

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation for legged/humanoid robots addressing underexplored gap in SSC literature with clear justification of unique challenges (gait jitter, 360° awareness, payload constraints)

Technically sound and coherent system design with well-justified components: dual-projection fusion balancing equirectangular continuity with raw annular texture, bi-grid voxelization elegantly combining Cartesian metric precision and cylindrical azimuthal coherence, GDC for feature-level motion correction without extra sensors

Comprehensive experimental validation including systematic component ablations (+0.39/+0.31/+0.41/+0.26 mIoU gains), FoV analysis demonstrating non-linear benefits of 360° ring closure, distance-binned analysis proving gains from far-range to near-field safety-critical regions, robustness across lighting/weather/cross-city shifts

Practical efficiency contributions: 30% parameter reduction vs MonoScene (101.76M vs 148.9M), 13.64 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin embedded platform with minimal overhead, deployable footprint making work actionable

Significant dataset contributions: QuadOcc with reproducible semi-automatic construction pipeline (LiDAR aggregation + Grounded-SAM + manual fixes), Human360Occ with dual-resolution support and within-/cross-city splits enabling systematic evaluation, extensive documentation facilitating future research

Honest and mature discussion of limitations including failure case analysis (Fig. 16) showing semantic brittleness under rare environment-weather combinations, explicit acknowledgment of data-driven model biases, discussion of sim-to-real gap with potential solutions

Strong experimental results surpassing LiDAR baseline (LMSCNet 18.44→20.56 mIoU on QuadOcc) and vision baseline (MonoScene 33.46→37.29 mIoU on H3O within-city), with code/dataset release promises and 11 pages of baseline implementation details enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited real-world data scope severely restricts generalization claims: only 10 campus scenes in QuadOcc (24K frames), no real humanoid data (H3O is purely CARLA-simulated), unaddressed sim-to-real gap means transferability to diverse deployments (indoor offices, forests, dynamic crowds, off-road terrain) remains unvalidated

Counterintuitive and concerning resolution scaling failure: increasing resolution from 64×64×8 to 128×128×16 degrades mIoU by 33% (32.23→21.16, Table 10), attributed vaguely to 'optimization difficulty' without investigation, suggests fundamental limitations when finer discretization needed for manipulation/grasping tasks

Persistent semantic misclassification under distribution shift indicates semantic understanding—not geometry—is limiting factor: Fig. 16 shows OneOcc still confuses vegetation with sidewalk despite geometric accuracy, paper acknowledges models are 'fundamentally data-driven' and inherit training biases, undermines practical reliability claims

Limited technical novelty in individual components: dual-projection is straightforward view combination, bi-grid voxelization combines known Cartesian+cylindrical ideas (Cylinder3D), AMoE-3D applies standard MoE with gradient-energy gating (incremental), GDC is simple 2D displacement MLP; contribution is primarily system design and application rather than algorithmic innovation

Unfair or unclear modality comparison: QuadOcc result (vision-only OneOcc beats LiDAR-based LMSCNet) conflates different sensor modalities without justification; while impressive on paper, comparing across modalities weakens the claimed breakthrough; H3O comparisons are fairer but only on synthetic data

Single-frame design fundamentally limits temporal reasoning: temporal aggregation (Sec. 6.7) adds only +0.36-0.48 mIoU with latency increase (69.93→78.60ms), GDC compensates for gait jitter but cannot model dynamic agents (pedestrians, robots), acknowledged but not adequately addressed for real-world scenarios

Modest GDC contribution with limited analysis: ablation shows only +0.39 mIoU improvement, qualitative analysis (Fig. 8) is illustrative but lacks comprehensive per-scenario breakdown, unclear when/why GDC helps or fails in practice

Dataset class imbalance not fully characterized or addressed: road dominates 52.3% of QuadOcc, sidewalk 26.24% of H3O, skew likely favors road-centric priors and masks performance on rare classes, no per-class failure mode analysis across environments
